chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyād, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Razīn, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام about the apostate, and he said:

"Whoever turns away from Islam and disbelieves in what was sent down upon Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم after his Islam, then there is no repentance for him, his killing has become obligatory, his wife is separated from him, and what he leaves behind is divided among his children."

key_terms.بَانَتْ مِنْهُ ٱمْرَأَتُهُ: his wife became separated from him
key_terms.رَغِبَ عَنِ ٱلْإِسْلَامِ: turned away from Islam and abandoned it
key_terms.فَلَا تَوْبَةَ لَهُ: no repentance is accepted for him in the legal ruling stated here
key_terms.كَفَرَ بِمَا أُنْزِلَ: disbelieved in what was revealed by Allah
key_terms.يُقْسَمُ مَا تَرَكَ: what he left behind is divided as inheritance
key_terms.ٱلْمُرْتَدِّ: the apostate; one who turns back from Islam after having accepted it

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith in Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām say about the ruling on the apostate?
ai.summary: This hadith records a legal ruling from Imam Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام concerning the one who turns away from Islam after having embraced it. It states the legal consequences mentioned here for apostasy, including the loss of marital bond and division of property among the children.
